examples.ko: 선생님이 시험 방법을 소상히 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher explained the exam format in detail.

examples.ko: 사고가 난 경위를 소상히 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me in detail how the accident happened.

examples.ko: 계약 내용을 소상히 알고 나서 서명했어요.
examples.en: I signed after learning the contract details thoroughly.

examples.ko: 담당자가 환불 절차를 소상히 안내해 줬어요.
examples.en: The person in charge explained the refund process in detail.

examples.ko: 그 일에 대해서는 제가 소상히 알지 못해요.
examples.en: I don't know the details of that matter.

examples.ko: 여행 일정을 소상히 적어서 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll write out the trip schedule in detail and send it to you.

explain: '자세히'와 뜻은 같지만 더 격식 있고 공식적인 느낌이에요. 편한 대화에서는 '자세히'가 더 자연스러워요. 설명하다, 밝히다, 알리다, 알다 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It means the same as '자세히' but sounds more formal and official. In casual talk '자세히' feels more natural. It goes well with verbs like 설명하다, 밝히다, 알리다 and 알다.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 실제 사건을 소설화한 작품이에요.
examples.en: This film is a work that fictionalizes a real event.

examples.ko: 작가가 할머니의 이야기를 소설화하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The writer wants to turn her grandmother's story into a novel.
She novelized that incident and published it as a book.
What would it feel like if this webtoon were turned into a novel?
I turned my friend's experience into a novel, and the response is good.

examples.ko: 역사 속 인물을 소설화하는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to turn a historical figure into a novel.

explain: 실제 사건이나 인물, 영화·웹툰 같은 이야기를 소설 형태로 바꿀 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '소설로 쓰다'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요. 결과물은 '소설화한 작품'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when you turn a real event, a person, or a story such as a film or webtoon into a novel. In daily talk people often say '소설로 쓰다' instead. The result is called a '소설화한 작품'.

examples.en: In this meeting, my opinion was in the minority.
We should respect the voice of the minority too.
He belongs to the minority faction within the party.

examples.ko: 소수파라고 해서 의견이 틀린 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being in the minority doesn't mean the opinion is wrong.

examples.ko: 투표에서 졌지만 소수파는 계속 문제를 제기했어요.
examples.en: They lost the vote, but the minority kept raising the issue.
In our class, that hobby is a minority one.

explain: 의견이나 집단에서 수가 적은 쪽을 말해요. 반대말은 '다수파'이고, 정치 뉴스와 회의 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 사람의 수가 적다는 느낌이 강하고, 의견 자체를 말할 때는 '소수 의견'도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the smaller side in an opinion or group. The opposite is '다수파', and it often appears in political news and talk about meetings. It stresses that the number of people is small; for the opinion itself you can also say '소수 의견'.

examples.en: The door suddenly opened and I was startled.
I flinched when I heard a noise behind me on the night road.
My sibling woke from a dream and sat up with a start.

examples.ko: 그는 전화벨 소리에 소스라쳐서 컵을 떨어뜨렸어요.
examples.en: He was so startled by the phone ringing that he dropped his cup.
I almost jumped out of my skin when I saw a snake at my feet.
My friend flinched as if startled.

explain: 주로 '소스라치게 놀라다' 꼴로 써요. '깜짝 놀라다'보다 몸이 움찔할 만큼 크게 놀랄 때 어울려요. 활용은 소스라쳐요, 소스라쳤어요예요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the form '소스라치게 놀라다'. Compared with '깜짝 놀라다', it fits a shock big enough to make your body flinch. The conjugations are 소스라쳐요 and 소스라쳤어요.

examples.en: I'm just an ordinary person.
The life of an ordinary person is precious in its own way.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 소시민 가족의 일상을 그렸어요.
examples.en: This novel depicts the daily life of an ordinary family.
When prices rise, ordinary people struggle the most.

examples.ko: 그는 소시민으로 조용히 살고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: He wanted to live quietly as an ordinary person.
I'm an ordinary person without big ambitions, so I'm content.

explain: 큰 권력이나 재산 없이 평범하게 사는 사람을 말해요. 자기를 낮추거나 약간 자조적으로 말할 때 쓰고, 작은 일상에만 매여 산다고 비판하는 말투로도 나와요. 남에게 쓸 때는 어감에 조심하세요.
explain_en: It means a person who lives an ordinary life without big power or wealth. People use it to humbly or wryly describe themselves, and sometimes in a critical tone about living only for small daily concerns. Be careful about the tone when using it for others.

examples.en: I'm a light eater, so one bowl is enough.
When I eat with a friend who eats little, food gets left over.

examples.ko: 우리 할머니는 소식가셔서 늘 조금만 드세요.
examples.en: My grandmother is a light eater, so she always eats just a little.
I naturally eat little, so buffets aren't great for me.
You eat so little. You're really a light eater.
My husband is a light eater, but he's very healthy.

explain: 반대말은 많이 먹는 사람을 뜻하는 '대식가'예요. 사람을 가리킬 때는 '소식가'를 쓰고, 적게 먹는 행동은 '소식하다'라고 해요. 보통 '저는 소식가예요'처럼 자기 식사량을 설명할 때 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '대식가', a big eater. Use '소식가' for the person, and '소식하다' for the act of eating little. It is typically used to describe your own appetite, as in '저는 소식가예요'.

examples.ko: 눈치 보지 말고 소신껏 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't mind others' reactions; say what you really believe.

examples.ko: 감독님은 선수들이 소신껏 뛰도록 믿어 줬어요.
examples.en: The coach trusted the players to play by their own convictions.

examples.ko: 저는 제 일을 소신껏 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to do my work according to my own convictions.

examples.ko: 결과는 신경 쓰지 말고 소신껏 결정하세요.
examples.en: Don't worry about the result; decide according to your own beliefs.

examples.ko: 그 의사는 환자를 위해 소신껏 치료했어요.
examples.en: That doctor treated the patient according to his own convictions.
I voted by my own conviction, so I have no regrets.

explain: '마음껏'은 하고 싶은 만큼 한다는 뜻이고, '소신껏'은 자기가 옳다고 믿는 대로 한다는 뜻이에요. 말하다, 행동하다, 결정하다, 일하다 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요. 응원하거나 조언할 때 '소신껏 하세요'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '마음껏' means as much as you like, while '소신껏' means doing what you believe is right. It goes well with verbs like 말하다, 행동하다, 결정하다 and 일하다. When cheering someone on or advising them, people often say '소신껏 하세요'.

examples.en: In my younger days, I was pretty good at soccer.

examples.ko: 소싯적 이야기를 하니 옛날 생각이 나요.
examples.en: Talking about my younger days brings back memories.
My father grew up in the countryside in his youth.

examples.ko: 내가 소싯적에 말이야, 매일 십 리를 걸었어요.
examples.en: Back in my day, I walked ten li every day.
I met my friends from my youth after a long time.
I heard my mother also sang well when she was young.

explain: 주로 나이 든 사람이 자기 젊은 시절을 떠올리며 '소싯적에'라고 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '젊었을 때', '어렸을 때'도 쓰는데, 소싯적은 옛날이야기를 하는 말투가 있어요. 어린 학생이 자기 이야기를 하면서 쓰면 조금 어색해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used by older people recalling their young days, as in '소싯적에'. You can also say '젊었을 때' or '어렸을 때', but 소싯적 has a tone of telling stories of the old days. It sounds a bit odd when a young student uses it about themselves.

examples.en: The river water swirls near the rocks.
The sea is churning because of the typhoon.
The water swirled and was sucked down the drain.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣자 마음속에서 분노가 소용돌이쳤어요.
examples.en: When I heard that, anger swirled inside me.

examples.ko: 커피에 우유를 부으니 소용돌이치는 모양이 예뻤어요.
examples.en: When I poured milk into the coffee, the swirling pattern looked pretty.

examples.ko: 온갖 생각이 머릿속에서 소용돌이쳐서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: All kinds of thoughts are swirling in my head, so I can't sleep.

explain: 물이나 바람이 빙글빙글 도는 모습에 쓰고, 감정이나 생각이 마음속에서 어지럽게 일어날 때도 비유로 써요. 명사 '소용돌이'에 '치다'가 붙은 말이라 활용은 소용돌이쳐요, 소용돌이쳤어요예요. 감정에 쓸 때는 분노, 혼란, 감동처럼 크고 강한 감정과 잘 맞아요.
explain_en: It describes water or wind spinning around, and is also used figuratively when emotions or thoughts stir wildly inside you. It is the noun '소용돌이' plus '치다', so the forms are 소용돌이쳐요 and 소용돌이쳤어요. For feelings it suits big, strong ones like anger, confusion or emotion.

examples.en: Children have a strong desire to own their toys.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 소유욕이 너무 커서 친구를 잃었어요.
examples.en: He was so possessive that he lost his friends.

examples.ko: 물건에 대한 소유욕 없이 가볍게 살아요.
examples.en: I live lightly, without a desire to own things.
Possessiveness makes a relationship uncomfortable when it goes too far.
Even puppies show possessiveness sometimes.
You shouldn't confuse possessiveness with love.

explain: 물건을 갖고 싶은 마음뿐 아니라 사람을 자기 곁에 두고 싶어 하는 마음에도 써요. '소유욕이 강하다', '소유욕이 없다'처럼 말하고, 사람에게 쓸 때는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 비슷한 '독점욕'은 혼자만 차지하고 싶은 마음에 더 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It covers not only wanting to own things but also wanting to keep a person close to you. People say '소유욕이 강하다' or '소유욕이 없다', and when used about people it sounds negative. The similar '독점욕' focuses more on wanting to have something all to yourself.

examples.en: If you get angry over something like that, you look petty.

examples.ko: 저는 소인배라서 작은 일도 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: I'm petty, so even small things bother me.
Please don't act so pettily.
He isn't a narrow-minded, petty person.

examples.ko: 남의 성공을 질투하는 건 소인배나 하는 일이에요.
examples.en: Only petty people envy other people's success.
Even if you call me petty, I can't help it.

explain: 마음이 좁고 그릇이 작은 사람을 낮춰 부르는 말이라, 남에게 직접 쓰면 욕이 돼요. 그래서 '제가 소인배라서요'처럼 자기를 낮출 때 더 자주 들려요. 인터넷에서는 반대 느낌으로 '대인배'라는 말도 써요.
explain_en: It belittles someone with a narrow mind, so saying it directly to another person is an insult. You more often hear it when people put themselves down, like '제가 소인배라서요'. Online, people also use '대인배' for the opposite, a big-hearted person.

examples.en: Since retiring, I tend a small garden as a pastime.
My grandfather is bored because he has nothing to pass the time.
Knitting is a good way for me to pass the time.
Try finding even a small pastime to get through the day.

examples.ko: 용돈도 벌 수 있는 소일거리를 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a light job that also earns some pocket money.
I go fishing every weekend to pass the time.

explain: 큰 목적 없이 시간을 보내려고 하는 가벼운 일을 말해요. '취미'보다 가볍고, 은퇴한 분이나 시간이 남는 사람의 작은 일에 잘 어울려요. '소일거리 삼아'라는 말투로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means a light activity you do just to pass the time, without any big purpose. It is lighter than '취미' (hobby) and suits small things done by retirees or people with spare time. The phrase '소일거리 삼아' (as a way to pass the time) is a common pattern.

examples.ko: 저는 맡은 소임을 끝까지 다하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to fulfill my assigned duty to the end.
I'm sorry I couldn't fulfill my duty as class president.
He is an employee who is faithful to his duties.
I'm nervous because I've taken on a new responsibility.
Everyone has their own role, so let's help each other.
A referee's duty is to make fair calls.

explain: '임무'와 비슷하지만 사람이 맡은 자리에서 해야 할 몫이라는 느낌이 강해요. '소임을 다하다', '소임을 맡다', '소임을 마치다'처럼 짝으로 많이 써요. 조금 무게 있는 말이라 일상 대화보다 연설이나 글에서 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is similar to '임무' but stresses the share of work a person must do in their position. It pairs with verbs as in '소임을 다하다', '소임을 맡다' and '소임을 마치다'. It sounds a bit weighty, so it suits speeches and writing more than casual talk.

examples.ko: 소자본으로 시작할 수 있는 가게를 찾아요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a shop I can start with little capital.
Small-capital startups are getting attention these days.

examples.ko: 소자본이라도 계획만 좋으면 해 볼 만해요.
examples.en: Even with little capital, it's worth trying if the plan is good.

examples.ko: 친구는 소자본을 모아 작은 카페를 열었어요.
examples.en: My friend pooled a small amount of capital and opened a little cafe.

examples.ko: 소자본 사업은 위험도 잘 따져야 해요.
examples.en: With a small-capital business, you must weigh the risks carefully too.
Please recommend a business item that suits a small budget.

explain: 장사나 창업에 들이는 돈이 적다는 뜻으로, 거의 '소자본 창업'처럼 써요. 반대말은 '대자본'이에요. 일상에서 돈이 적다고 말할 때는 쓰지 않고, 사업 이야기에서 써요.
explain_en: It means little money is put into a business, and it is mostly used as '소자본 창업' (small-capital startup). The opposite is '대자본'. You don't use it for everyday money talk, only when discussing business.

examples.en: Long ago, my great-grandfather was a tenant farmer.

examples.ko: 소작농은 수확한 곡식의 일부를 땅 주인에게 냈어요.
examples.en: Tenant farmers gave part of the harvested grain to the landowner.
We learned about the life of tenant farmers in history class.

examples.ko: 그 소설은 가난한 소작농 가족의 이야기예요.
examples.en: That novel is about a poor tenant-farming family.

examples.ko: 농지 개혁으로 많은 소작농이 자기 땅을 갖게 됐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to land reform, many tenant farmers came to own their own land.
The tenant farmers joined forces and made their voices heard.

explain: 남의 땅을 빌려 농사를 짓는 농민을 말해요. 자기 땅에서 농사짓는 사람은 '자작농'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 지금 일상보다는 역사 수업이나 옛날 배경의 소설에서 만나요.
explain_en: It refers to a farmer who rents someone else's land to farm. It helps to learn it with its counterpart '자작농', a farmer who farms their own land. You meet it in history lessons and in novels set in the past more than in modern daily life.

examples.en: The party's young reformers demanded reform.
He is called one of the young scholars in academia.
The young lawmakers gathered and held a press conference.
At a company too, the opinions of the younger faction matter.
There is conflict between the young faction and the elders.
Young directors called the new guard are getting attention.

explain: 어떤 조직이나 분야에서 젊고 개혁적인 사람들을 가리켜요. 나이 많은 쪽은 '원로'나 '중진'이라고 해서 대비해서 자주 나와요. 주로 정치나 학계 뉴스에서 보는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to the young, reform-minded people within an organization or field. It is often contrasted with the older side, called '원로' or '중진'. You mostly see it in political or academic news.

examples.en: In class, we split into small groups and discussed.
In small-group activities, everyone shares an opinion.

examples.ko: 우리 소집단은 네 명으로 이루어져 있어요.
examples.en: Our small group consists of four people.
Please prepare presentations for each small group.

examples.ko: 저는 큰 모임보다 소집단 모임이 편해요.
examples.en: I'm more comfortable with small-group meetings than big ones.
The students divided roles within the small group.

explain: 반대말은 '대집단'이고, 수업이나 연구에서 '소집단 토론', '소집단 활동'처럼 많이 써요. 한국 교실에서는 같은 뜻으로 '모둠'이라는 말도 써요. 일상에서 친구 모임을 말할 때는 보통 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: The opposite is '대집단', and it is often used in class or research as in '소집단 토론' and '소집단 활동'. In Korean classrooms the word '모둠' is also used with the same meaning. It isn't normally used for casual groups of friends.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 가까운 곳에서 소쩍새가 울었어요.
examples.en: When the rain stopped, a scops owl called nearby.
Every night I hear a scops owl from the mountain.
Scops owls rest in the day and are active at night.

examples.ko: 시골 할머니 댁에서 소쩍새 울음을 처음 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a scops owl's call for the first time at my grandmother's countryside house.
I've never seen a scops owl in person.
I recorded the sound of a scops owl calling.

explain: 올빼미 종류의 작은 새로, 밤에 울어서 소리로 먼저 알게 되는 경우가 많아요. 울음소리를 '소쩍소쩍'으로 흉내 내요. 시나 노래, 소설의 시골 밤 장면에 나오기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a small owl-type bird, and since it calls at night you often notice it by sound first. Its call is imitated as '소쩍소쩍'. It sometimes appears in poems, songs and country night scenes in novels.

examples.ko: 안내 소책자를 한 권 받아 왔어요.
examples.en: I picked up one information booklet.
The museum hands out free booklets.

examples.ko: 이 소책자에 사용 방법이 다 나와 있어요.
examples.en: All the instructions are in this booklet.
If you make it into a booklet, it's easy to carry around.
I downloaded the school introduction booklet from the website.
I planned the itinerary using a travel booklet.

explain: 얇고 작은 책을 말하고, 안내나 설명을 담은 것에 많이 써요. 광고나 홍보용은 '팸플릿'이나 '브로슈어'라고도 해요. 보통 '안내 소책자', '무료 소책자'처럼 앞에 말이 붙어요.
explain_en: It means a thin, small book, often one with guidance or explanations. Promotional ones are also called '팸플릿' or '브로슈어'. It usually comes with a word in front, like '안내 소책자' or '무료 소책자'.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 소탈해서 팬들과 편하게 사진을 찍어요.
examples.en: That actor is down-to-earth, so he takes photos with fans casually.
Our boss is unpretentious, so he often eats with the staff.
Thanks to his easygoing personality, he has many friends.
Even though he's famous, his style is simple and unfussy.
I like seeing his unaffected smile.
My grandmother is down-to-earth and warm-hearted.

explain: 꾸밈없고 털털해서 대하기 편한 성격을 칭찬할 때 써요. '털털하다'와 비슷하지만 조금 더 점잖은 칭찬이라서, 유명한 사람이나 윗사람이 권위를 내세우지 않을 때 잘 어울려요. 흉이 아니라 좋은 뜻으로만 써요.
explain_en: It praises a person who is unpretentious and easygoing, making them comfortable to be around. It is similar to '털털하다' but a slightly more refined compliment, which fits famous people or superiors who don't show off their authority. It is used only in a good sense, never as criticism.

examples.en: Prices rose slightly this month.
The stock price fell slightly and then recovered.
I saw news that the exchange rate rose slightly.
My score went up slightly from last time.
The temperature dropped a little, so the mornings are chilly.
My salary was raised slightly this year.

explain: 뉴스나 경제 기사에서 오르다, 내리다, 상승하다, 하락하다 앞에 자주 붙어요. 반대말은 '대폭'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '조금'이나 '약간'이 더 편해요.
explain_en: It often sits before verbs like 오르다, 내리다, 상승하다 and 하락하다 in news and economic articles. The opposite is '대폭'. In daily conversation, '조금' or '약간' feels more natural.
